title: Peter Martyr: grace as favour toward the elect, and as the gifts it gives
source_text: II. Et ita quoque Petrus Martyr in locis communibus, Nomen, inquit, gratiae in sacra scriptura bifariam accipitur. Primum quidem & praecipue significat Dei erga homines benevolentiam & gratuitum favorem quo prosequitur Electos. Deinde quia Deus Electos suos praeclaris donis afficit, gratia interdum significat ea etiam dona quae nobis a Deo gratis conferuntur. Classe 3. loco 2. paragr. 7.
pass_a_gloss: II. And so also Peter Martyr in the commonplaces, The name, he says, of grace is taken in sacred scripture in two ways. First indeed and chiefly it signifies the benevolence of God toward men and the free favour by which he follows the Elect. Then because God affects his Elect with excellent gifts, grace sometimes signifies also those gifts which are conferred on us by God freely. Class 3. place 2. paragr. 7.
pass_b_english: Thesis II. Peter Martyr says the same in his Commonplaces. The word grace, he writes, is used in two ways in holy scripture. First and chiefly it means God's goodwill toward people and the free favour with which he pursues the elect.
Then, because God endows his elect with outstanding gifts, grace sometimes also means the gifts that God bestows on us freely (class 3, locus 2, paragraph 7).

choices.why: Tilenus's terms: grace as God's own favour (active) and grace as a gift received (passive).
